paragraphs: Rav Bibi ben Abaye. Chananel’s commentary, at פרק א״ל המנונה [chapter wording unresolved]: tzeirei/chirik; Arukh: tzeirei/kamatz. Priest descended from Eli. Heilprin’s text and the Arukh name Rav Pappa. Heilprin proposes Rav Pappi, who called him Memullai, Yevamot 75, end of b; Ketubbot 85a; Eruvin 25b; Bava Metzia 109a: “Since you come from Memullai, you say words that are muliyyata?” Bava Batra 137b, 151a: Huna bar Rav Yehoshua similarly; Rashbam: place name, insulting him. Eruvin 51b: Bei Mammal’s people; Arukh, Mamla, place, Bereshit Rabbah 59: Meir went to Mamla, saw them black-haired, etc., and said to them: “Perhaps you are descended from Eli?” Puzzling: Pappi calls him master, Rashi, teacher, Chullin 43b—why insult? Rashi, Eruvin: cut short; Bava Metzia: hard mound; see Tosafot, Yevamot, and Rashi, Ketubbot’s alternatives. Prefer the Gaon in Arukh, seventh mal entry: a great man speaking great things; see Shnei Luchot Habberit and Beit Yehudah. Rama of Fano: moral rebuke—“By sacrifice and meal offering it is not atoned, but it is atoned through words of Torah”; therefore one should take particular care to repair the damage. He considered completing the entire year’s portions on the eve of Yom Kippur, Berakhot 8b; Arukh, kol. Sought to see demons, was harmed, healed through prayer, Berakhot 6a. The Angel of Death frequently visited him and told him of an incident long before: he told his messenger, “Bring me Miriam the women’s hairdresser.” The messenger brought Miriam who reared children, Chagigah 4b. Ein Yaakov’s Dimi bar Abaye is erroneous. Bibi bar Abaye asked, etc.; Kahana: “Is not this Rami bar Chama’s?” Bibi: “Did I come later and dispute?”, Eruvin 90a. Acha bar Ika and Acha bar Rava in his name. He spoke to Huna bar Rav Yehoshua, Sanhedrin 66b; see above. Rav Zutri bar Tuvya’s mother came before him. Chiyya bar Rav of Difti recited to him. Kahana, see above. He spoke to Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak, Berakhot 6b; Rabbah bar Ulla called him teacher.
